newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's GrainCorp sets up market in its shares.
newsitem.headline: Australia's GrainCorp sets up market in its shares.

text.p: New South Wales (NSW) grain handling group GrainCorp Operations Ltd said on Tuesday it had established an exempt stock market for its shareholders.

"The decision to allow trading on the exempt market means GrainCorp shareholders will now find it easier to find buyers for their GrainCorp shares and for buyers to locate willing sellers," GrainCorp said.
Morgan Stockbroking Ltd has been appointed to operate the market and independent supervision will be conducted by accountancy firm Coopers and Lybrand, it said.
Trading is expected to begin in early June.
Graincorp, an unlisted public company, was privatised in September 1992 by the Prime Wheat Association Ltd (PWA), a company limited by guarantee.
Shares in GrainCorp were issued about a year later.
The PWA will retain a Foundation Share in GrainCorp, effectively giving NSW graingrowers control of the organisation through its six nominated board members.
There are currently in excess of 3,000 shareholders entitled to GrainCorp voting and dividend rights, GrainCorp said.

GrainCorp evolved from the NSW state government's former Grain Handling Authority and runs grain handling and storage at country receival points and at the port terminals at Port Kembla and Newcastle.

Legislation covering so-called exempt stock markets allows unlisted public companies, many of which in Australia evolved from rural co-operatives, to establish a formal mechanism for trading in their shares.
But GrainCorp said it is only the second company in Australia ever to do so. It did not name the other one.
